Carey Jr.''' (born February 25, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He finished his high school career at [[NSU University School]] as a five-star recruit and among the top-ranked players in the 2019 class.{{cite web |url=http://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/index.ssf/2018/01/vernon_carey_jr_recruiting_top.html |title=Vernon Carey Jr. recruiting: Top 2019 prospect to make first official visit to Michigan State in February (photos/video)|date=January 16, 2018 }} ==High school career== Carey starred for four years at [[University School of Nova Southeastern University]] in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]]. During his freshman season, he averaged 18.0 points, 7.0 rebounds and 2.0 blocks while leading the Sharks to a 15–9 overall record. As a sophomore, Carey averaged 22.0 points and 8.0 rebounds per game, while leading his team to a 20–7 record and a Florida district state championship. After his sophomore year, Carey was named to the 2017 [[Miami Herald]] and [[Sun Sentinel]] all-district teams as well as 2017 MaxPreps All-American honorable mention. As a junior, Carey averaged 26.0 points and 10.1 rebounds a game, while leading the Sharks to an overall record of 36–2, the 2018 Florida 5A state championship, and championships at the 2017 City of Palms Invitational and the 2017 John Wall Invitational.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/699672/2018/12/06/the-birth-of-vernon-carey-jr-duke-recruit/|title=The Birth of Vernon Carey Jr|last=Quinn|first=Brendan|date=December 6, 2018|work=theathletic.com|access-date=November 24, 2019}} Carey led his team to the finals at the High School National Tournament, losing in the championship game to [[Montverde Academy]] and its star, [[RJ Barrett]].{{Cite news |last=Lammer |first=Pat |date=December 14, 2018 |title=Montverde rolls over University School for Geico Nationals title |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-geico-nationals-championship-0331-story.html |access-date=March 31, 2018 |work=orlandosentinel.com}} Carey averaged 17.4 points and 5.3 rebounds per game on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) Circuit for his AAU team, Nike Team Florida.{{Cite news|url=https://www.d1circuit.com/roster_players/178203403.html|title=Vernon Carey Jr EYBL stats|work=d1circuit.com|access-date=December 6, 2018}} Carey finished his senior season averaging 21.7 [[points per game|points]], 9.0 [[rebounds per game|rebounds]] and 1.1 blocks per game.{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/09/13/duke-blue-devils-vernon-carey-recruiting|title=Duke expecting big things from five-star big man Vernon Carey Jr|last=Caron|first=Emily|date=September 13, 2019|work=si.com|access-date=November 24, 2019}} The 2018–19 University team with a supporting cast of [[Scottie Barnes]], [[Taylor Hendricks]], Jace Howard and [[Jett Howard]], successfully defended its [[FHSSA]] Class 5A State championship with a victory over [[Andrew Jackson High School (Jacksonville)|Andrew Jackson High School]], despite Carey being sidelined for the championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/picture-gallery/news/local/2019/03/07/class-5a-final-university-72/66145967007/|title=Class 5A Final: University 72,
